next_state_election.name: State Election
next_state_election.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: 2026 State Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Massachusetts's November 3, 2026 State Election is October 24, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — How to Vote Early
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 17–30: Massachusetts provides no-excuse early in-person voting for the November 3, 2026 State Election from October 17 through October 30. Each city and town establishes its own early-voting locations and daily schedule.

glance_notes.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Voting by Mail
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Vote by Mail: Any registered Massachusetts voter may request a Vote by Mail ballot for the November 3, 2026 State Election without providing an excuse. The application must reach the local election office by 5:00 p.m. on October 27.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Massachusetts residents may register online, by mail or in person. Massachusetts also provides automatic voter registration through certain transactions with agencies including the Registry of Motor Vehicles, MassHealth and the Massachusetts Health Connector. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, a Massachusetts resident and at least 16 years old. Residents ages 16 and 17 may pre-register, but generally must be at least 18 years old to vote. A person currently incarcerated for a felony conviction is not eligible to vote while incarcerated. Eligible residents may register again after release.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, in person or automatic registration
register.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Registering to Vote
register.internal_note: The Secretary of the Commonwealth directly establishes online, mail and in-person registration and Massachusetts's automatic voter-registration system. Massachusetts permits pre-registration beginning at age 16. Current Massachusetts law disqualifies people while incarcerated for a felony conviction but not after release. Do not incorrectly extend the restriction to probation or parole.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Massachusetts's official voter registration lookup to verify your registration status, party enrollment, polling location and other voter information. Voters should check their record after moving or changing their name and contact their local election office if information needs to be corrected.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the state voter lookup
check_registration.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Voter Registration Status
check_registration.internal_note: The Massachusetts Elections Division provides an official voter-registration status lookup through its voter services system. Local election offices maintain registration records and can correct or update records when appropriate.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The voter registration deadline for Massachusetts's November 3, 2026 State Election is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Voters should also make necessary registration changes by this deadline. Massachusetts does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Upcoming Elections
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 Upcoming Elections page directly identifies October 24 as the voter registration deadline for the November 3 State Election. Massachusetts generally closes registration 10 days before state elections. There is no general same-day registration procedure for the November State Election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Massachusetts voters can use the Secretary of the Commonwealth's official voter information service to find their assigned Election Day polling place. Each voting precinct has an assigned polling location, and voters casting a ballot on Election Day must vote at the polling place assigned to their precinct. During early voting, voters may use any early voting location in the city or town where they are registered.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned precinct polling place
polling_place.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Where Do I Vote?
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary's When, Where, How Do I Vote guidance directly states that Massachusetts is divided into precincts, each precinct has an assigned polling place, and Election Day voters must use their assigned polling place. Supporting official source: [https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/voter-resources/when-where-how-do-i-vote.htm](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/voter-resources/when-where-how-do-i-vote.htm).

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Massachusetts's State Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places statewide are open from at least 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m., although cities and towns may choose to open as early as 5:45 a.m. Voters who are in line when the polls close are entitled to vote. Election Day voters must use their assigned precinct polling place. Massachusetts does not require every voter to present identification; identification is required only in certain circumstances.
election_day.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — When, Where, How Do I Vote?
election_day.internal_note: The Secretary directly confirms 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. statewide state-election hours, local authority to open as early as 5:45 a.m., the right of voters already in line at closing to vote, and the assigned-precinct rule. November 3, 2026 is independently confirmed by the official Upcoming Elections page.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: For the November 3, 2026 State Election, every Massachusetts polling place is open from at least 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Cities and towns may choose to open their polling places earlier, as early as 5:45 a.m. Voters should check with their local election office for their community's exact opening time. Anyone in line when the polls close at 8:00 p.m. may still vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Polling Hours
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary's current polling-hours page directly establishes 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for state elections and permits cities and towns to open as early as 5:45 a.m. The in-line-at-closing protection is confirmed by the official When, Where, How Do I Vote page.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Massachusetts provides no-excuse early in-person voting for statewide elections. For the November 3, 2026 State Election, early voting runs from October 17 through October 30. At least one early voting site is provided in every community, and voters may use any early voting location in the city or town where they are registered. Daily hours and locations are established locally. The Secretary of the Commonwealth is scheduled to publish community-specific General Election early-voting schedules no later than October 9.
early_voting.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — How to Vote Early
early_voting.internal_note: The current official early-voting page directly establishes October 17-30 for the 2026 State Election, states that no excuse is required, guarantees at least one site per community and allows voters to use any early-voting location within their registered city or town. It states that November 3 schedules and locations will be posted no later than October 9, so this section should be reverified after publication.

absentee_mail.label: Vote by Mail & Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Massachusetts provides no-excuse Vote by Mail for state elections, so any registered voter may request a mail-in ballot for the November 3, 2026 State Election. Applications may be submitted online or sent to the voter's local election office by mail, email or fax. The application must reach the local election office by 5:00 p.m. on October 27. Completed ballots may be returned by mail, delivered to the local election office, placed in an authorized ballot drop box, or returned at an early voting location during early-voting hours. A ballot cannot be returned to an Election Day polling place. For the November biennial State Election, a ballot returned by mail may arrive up to three days after Election Day if it is postmarked by Election Day. Ballots returned in person or by drop box must be received by the close of polls on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; apply by 5:00 p.m. October 27
absentee_mail.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current Secretary page directly establishes no-excuse Vote by Mail, application methods, the fifth-business-day application deadline, ballot return options, the prohibition on Election Day polling-place drop-off and the special three-day arrival period for mailed ballots in biennial November state elections if postmarked by Election Day. The official 2026 Upcoming Elections page specifically establishes October 27 at 5:00 p.m. as the application deadline.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Massachusetts does not require every voter to show identification at the polls. A voter may be required to provide identification when voting for the first time in Massachusetts, when listed as an inactive voter, when casting a provisional or challenged ballot, or when an election worker has a practical and legal reason to request identification. Acceptable identification must show the voter's name and registered address and can include a driver's license, state identification card, recent utility bill, rent receipt or lease, voter registration document, letter from a school dormitory or housing office, or another printed document containing the voter's name and address. Photo identification is not generally required.
voter_id.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Identification Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary page directly identifies the circumstances in which identification may be required and provides the acceptable-document examples. Massachusetts does not have a general photo-ID-at-the-polls requirement. A first-time Massachusetts voter required to show identification who cannot provide it may cast a provisional ballot and must return with identification before polls close for that ballot to count.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Massachusetts requires polling locations to be accessible to voters with disabilities and provides accessible voting procedures and equipment. Voters may choose someone to assist them with entering the polling place, checking in, entering the voting booth, preparing the ballot or leaving the polling place, subject to federal restrictions on assistance by an employer or union representative. Accessible voting equipment is available for voters who want to mark their ballot privately and independently. Massachusetts also provides accessible Vote by Mail accommodations for voters who cannot independently mark a paper ballot because of a disability.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible locations, assistance and voting equipment
accessible_voting.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary directly states that polling locations must be accessible and describes voter assistance rights. Massachusetts provides accessible voting equipment in polling locations and accommodations for voters who cannot independently use ordinary paper mail ballots. Elections Division accessibility contact information includes 1-800-462-VOTE and TTY 1-800-720-3480.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Massachusetts provides special voting procedures for eligible active-duty military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Military and overseas voters covered by federal law are exempt from Massachusetts's ordinary voter registration requirement and may apply directly for an absentee ballot. The Federal Post Card Application may be used to request ballots. Voters may choose to receive their ballot through an online portal, by fax or by mail and may return the completed ballot electronically, by fax or by mail under the procedures and deadlines that apply to military and overseas voters. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup when necessary.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery/return and FWAB available
military_overseas.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The current Secretary page directly states that military and overseas voters are exempt from Massachusetts registration requirements, confirms absentee-ballot eligibility, and permits ballot delivery through an online portal, fax or mail. It also expressly permits return by email/online, fax or mail and provides FWAB as a backup. Military/overseas deadlines differ according to election and return method, so ordinary Vote by Mail deadlines should not be applied to these voters.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students who consider Massachusetts their voting residence may register using a qualifying Massachusetts address, including a campus residence when it is the student's legal voting residence. Students who remain registered at another qualifying residence may vote according to the rules that apply to that registration. A Massachusetts voter who needs to show identification may use a letter from a school dormitory or housing office showing the voter's name and registered address as an acceptable form of identification. Students should maintain only one voting residence and may not vote in more than one jurisdiction in the same election.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying Massachusetts residence
student_voting.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Identification Requirements
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary's identification guidance expressly accepts a letter from a school dormitory or housing office showing the voter's name and registered address when identification is required. Massachusetts voter eligibility is residence-based. The reader-facing language deliberately avoids implying that merely attending a Massachusetts college automatically establishes Massachusetts voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Massachusetts voters can use the Secretary of the Commonwealth's official voter information tools to view the sample ballot for their precinct when it becomes available. Ballot contents vary by city or town, precinct, legislative district and local contests, so voters should use their residential address to retrieve the appropriate ballot. A sample ballot is provided for information and is not an official ballot that can be cast.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your precinct's sample ballot online
sample_ballot.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Where Do I Vote?
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary's voter-information system provides precinct-specific sample ballots. Current 2026 State Primary sample ballots are already published through this system and expressly state that they are not valid official ballots and that additional local offices may appear. General Election samples should be reverified after the September 1 primary and ballot certification.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Elections Division, 1 Ashburton Place, Room 1705, Boston, MA 02108. Toll-free voter information line: 1-800-462-VOTE (8683). Phone: 617-727-2828. Fax: 617-742-3238. Email: elections@sec.state.ma.us. Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:45 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Local election offices can assist with voter registration, polling places, Vote by Mail, ballot drop boxes and local election questions.
contact.source_name: Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The current official contact page directly verifies the Elections Division address, toll-free number, 617-727-2828 phone number, 617-742-3238 fax, [elections@sec.state.ma.us](mailto:elections@sec.state.ma.us) email address and weekday 8:45 a.m.-5:00 p.m. hours. The email is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth Elections Division website for official statewide information about voter registration, election dates, early voting, Vote by Mail, Election Day voting, accessibility and military and overseas voting. The state's voter information tools provide registration status, polling-place and sample-ballot information. Local city and town election offices administer voter registration records, local early-voting schedules, polling locations, mail ballots and ballot drop boxes.

official_resources.internal_note: Official 2026 election information: [https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/recent-updates/upcoming-elections.htm](https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/recent-updates/upcoming-elections.htm).
